name: Single-Leg Balance
description: Stand on one foot, other foot off the floor, and hold. Keep the standing knee soft and let the foot and ankle do the correcting rather than the hip. Progress by closing the eyes, which removes vision and forces the ankle's own position sense to do the work, then by standing on a folded towel or a cushion. Balance is proprioception, and proprioception is what an ankle sprain actually damages — the loss of it is the strongest predictor of spraining the same ankle again. Costs nothing and can be done while brushing teeth or waiting for coffee. Compare sides; the previously injured ankle is usually noticeably worse and that gap is the thing being closed.
